Product photos / FIELD GUIDE

JPG vs PNG vs WebP: a seller’s practical image guide

The best image format is the one that keeps the important detail and works where your customer will see it.

By Manglo Editorial6 November 20267 min read
THE MANGLO PLAYBOOK / ORIGINAL GUIDE

You have finished the product shoot. Now you need a listing thumbnail, a transparent badge and an image for your own store. Should each file be a JPG, PNG or WebP? There is no universal winner. These formats make different trade-offs between compatibility, transparency and compression.

The short decision table

Use caseUsually start withWhy
Standard product photographJPGBroad listing compatibility; manageable file sizes
Product photograph on your own websiteWebPEfficient delivery where supported
Transparent logo or graphicPNG or WebPPreserves transparent areas
Marketplace with a stated format requirementThat required formatAcceptance matters more than theoretical efficiency

JPG: the practical photograph default

JPEG uses lossy compression, so lower quality settings can introduce visible blocks and smearing. It is widely accepted and works well for photographic subjects. It cannot preserve transparency. White-background product photographs are a common fit, provided the marketplace permits them and you check small print after export.

PNG: clean graphics and transparency

PNG is lossless for the stored pixel data, which is useful for typography, logos, diagrams and illustrations with crisp edges. But lossless does not mean every PNG looks better: a blurry source remains blurry, and a photographic PNG can be unnecessarily large. PNG does not recover original quality after prior lossy compression.

WebP: efficient for the web

WebP supports both lossy and lossless encoding and can preserve alpha transparency. On websites that serve WebP successfully it is often an efficient option. However, an upload form or older workflow may impose different requirements. Always verify what your destination accepts rather than assuming browser support means marketplace support.

Make a fair comparison with your own photo

  1. Keep the same source image and output dimensions.
  2. Export a JPG and a WebP at comparable visual quality; export PNG if the use case needs it.
  3. Compare actual file sizes and examine fine details at 100% zoom.
  4. Check transparency, color, text and the destination upload.
  5. Pick the smallest acceptable file—not simply the smallest number.

There are no benchmark results in this article because file size depends on the actual image and encoder settings. You can make an evidence-based choice with your own products using the Manglo image converter.

A simple rule for sellers

Export for the destination, keep originals, and check the finished asset. If you sell across countries or channels, store separate export copies so you do not accidentally upload a web-optimized format where a platform expects JPG.
